title: Rclone or rsync: Syncing Files to the Cloud vs Between Servers
excerpt: rsync is the classic tool for efficient file copying between local systems and over SSH; Rclone brings a similar experience to dozens of cloud storage services. Many administrators keep both.
verdict: Choose Rclone when your files move to and from cloud storage such as S3-compatible buckets, Google Drive or OneDrive. Choose rsync for fast, efficient copies between servers or local disks, where its delta-transfer algorithm is hard to beat.

spec1.label: Cloud storage support
spec1.device1Value: Talks directly to dozens of cloud storage services
spec1.device2Value: Designed for local filesystems and SSH transfers

spec2.label: History and stability
spec2.device1Value: Younger, but mature for its purpose
spec2.device2Value: One of the oldest and most proven sync tools on Unix-like systems

spec3.label: Speed for large local files
spec3.device2Value: Highly optimised, sending only the changed parts of files
